raw_response:
I have been farming this land in Quzhou for over forty years. My father grew wheat and corn here, and his father before him. The North China Plain soil is good for these crops, and I know them well. I am not going to try something new at my age — cotton prices have been unstable, and I don't have the energy for vegetables on a large scale anymore. My knees aren't what they were.

I have about 8 mu of flat irrigated land. I will do the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, the same as every year. I plant wheat in October after the rains, and after harvest in June I seed corn right away into the stubble — no need to plow again.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed from the township supply cooperative, Jimai-series, whatever they have. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and urea at jointing stage. I irrigate three times: once before planting to wet the bed, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray once for rust and once for aphids when I see them. I use the rotary tiller to prepare the seedbed.

For maize, I use a hybrid — Zhengdan 958, I've used it for years. I seed it without tilling, straight into the wheat stubble. Summer rains usually handle irrigation but I pump once if July is dry. I spray for corn borer when the extension station says to.

I keep a small kitchen garden behind the house for vegetables, but that is not a crop — that is just eating.
